{"id": "25595811-b0a1-47f2-8937-1a40ceecc326", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The cause is the security group. Nothing allows inbound SSH (TCP 22) to these instances, so connection attempts time out.

**What I checked, for all three instances (`i-1234567890abcdef0_1`, `i-1234567890abcdef0_2`, `i-1234567890abcdef0_3`)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Instance state and status checks | All running, with instance and system checks passing and no scheduled events. |
| Public IP | Each instance has one, in subnet `subnet-4fe1f806`. |
| Routing | The main route table has `0.0.0.0/0` through the internet gateway `igw-ea7c458d`, and it's active. |
| Network ACL | The default ACL allows all inbound and outbound traffic. |
| **Security group** | **All three use the `default` group `sg-a8544cd4`. Its only inbound rule allows all traffic from members of the same group. There is no rule for port 22 from any IP range.** |

Nothing is wrong with the instances or the network path. The security group drops your SSH packets, which looks like a timeout rather than a "connection refused".

**A second problem you'd hit next:** none of the three instances has an EC2 key pair attached. Once port 22 is open, key-based SSH still won't work unless you've set up keys another way, such as in the AMI or through user data.

**Ways to fix it**
1. **Use SSM Session Manager.** All three instances have the `AmazonSSMRoleForInstancesQuickSetup` instance profile. If the SSM agent is online, you can open a shell without port 22 or keys, and no security group change is needed.
2. **Add an inbound rule for TCP 22.** I'd limit it to your own IP or your corporate CIDR, not `0.0.0.0/0`. This is the default group, so any rule I add applies to every instance and ENI that uses it. Creating a dedicated SSH security group and attaching it to the instance you need would be cleaner.

If you want me to add the rule, tell me which instance you're trying to reach and the source CIDR to allow (for example `203.0.113.10/32`). The change needs your approval before it runs. I can also check whether these instances show up as online in SSM first.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
